Definition: from G5384 and G5424; friendly of mind, i.e. kind:--courteous.
BiblicalUsage: Philophron means friendly of mind, courteous, and it appears once, in Peter's call to unity. He tells the brethren to be all of one mind, having compassion one of another, and to love as brethren, to be pitiful and courteous.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that courtesy is the smallest fruit of the Spirit and one of the most convincing: a courteous church is a believable church.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
